page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine designed for intensive machine learning and parallel computing workloads. The system pairs dual NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing 160 GB of aggregate VRAM with 52 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 26 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 105 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), and vector AES. Complementing the compute architecture is 468.0 GB of system memory (9.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 1608 GB local NVMe SSD volume.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution rates in AI-centric workloads. In small (135M) model LLM inference, the configuration achieves 10,254.62 tokens per second for prompt processing and 350.02 tokens per second during generation. When running a medium 7B model, performance registers at 5,644.37 tokens per second for prompts and 194.27 tokens per second for generation, placing both results in the top 10 percent tier. System memory throughput is similarly high, with cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaching 3,828.33 GB/sec and uncached 256 MB reads achieving 214.57 GB/sec.

General-purpose compute and auxiliary benchmarks show robust figures, such as a PassMark CPU score of 54,314.03 and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 2,079.0 and 17,415.0, respectively. While stress-ng execution sits within the middle 50 percent category, specialized metrics like bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (302.55 GB/sec) and database operations reflect strong results. By integrating substantial NVMe storage with dual enterprise-grade accelerators, this instance delivers high compute density, making it suitable for distributed deep learning training, medium-sized LLM fine-tuning and inference pipelines, high-throughput batch processing, and demanding data analytics.
